definitions.explanation: Meat that has been finely chopped or ground using a grinder. Used as an ingredient in dishes such as hamburgers, meatballs, and gyoza.

examples.japanese: {挽肉|ひきにく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}って→買う：00489_kau⟧きて。
⟦{豚|ぶた}→豚：04710_buta⟧{挽肉|ひきにく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{餃子|ぎょうざ}→餃子：08634_gyouza⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made gyoza with ground pork.

examples.japanese: {挽肉|ひきにく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{炒|いた}めて→炒める：01879_itameru⟧、⟦そぼろ→そぼろ：10383_soboro⟧{丼|どん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I stir-fried ground meat and vegetables to make soboro donburi.

notes:
Also commonly written in hiragana as ⟦ひき{肉|にく}→ひき肉：17241_hikiniku⟧ or in katakana as ⟦ひき{肉|にく}→ひき肉：17241_hikiniku⟧. The kanji ⟦{挽|ひ}く→挽く：12794_hiku⟧ means to grind.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {牛|ぎゅう}{挽肉|ひきにく} (ground beef)
- ⟦{豚|ぶた}→豚：04710_buta⟧{挽肉|ひきにく} (ground pork)
- {鶏|とり}{挽肉|ひきにく} (ground chicken)
- {合|あ}い{挽|び}き⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧ (mixed ground meat, usually beef and pork)

SUPERMARKET LABELS:
At Japanese supermarkets, ground meat is typically labeled by animal: ⟦{牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく}→牛ひき肉：23362_gyuuhikiniku⟧, ⟦{豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}→豚ひき肉：23445_butahikiniku⟧, ⟦{鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}→鶏ひき肉：23444_torihikiniku⟧, or ⟦{合|あ}いびき{肉|にく}→合いびき肉：22856_aibikiniku⟧.
